title: Free Recall with Open-Loop Stimulation at Encoding
description: This dataset contains behavioral events and intracranial EEG recordings from a delayed free recall task in which participants studied visually presented word lists, completed arithmetic distractor problems, and then freely recalled the words. Open-loop electrical stimulation was delivered during encoding to single electrodes in the hippocampus and entorhinal cortex, on alternating two-word blocks in 20 of 25 lists per session. Data were collected at multiple clinical sites in collaboration with the Computational Memory Lab at the University of Pennsylvania.
methods_description: Participants with implanted intracranial electrodes performed delayed free recall. Stimulation started 200 ms before the first word of a block and lasted 4.6 s, with no stimulation during distractor or retrieval phases. Stimulation parameters (anode/cathode, amplitude, frequency, pulse width, pulse count) are recorded in the events files. Recordings are provided in monopolar and bipolar montages, from Blackrock and Medtronic systems, scaled to volts.
